title: Around the World from Woodbridge
subtitle: Heading east  ·  4 drives  ·  3 flights  ·  back home to Woodbridge
intro: This is your trip around the world, from Woodbridge, Virginia, heading east and back home again: about nineteen and a half thousand miles, with four drives and three flights.
outro: And you're home in Woodbridge. That's the whole world in one loop: about four thousand seven hundred miles by car and fourteen thousand eight hundred in the air.

holds.text: First, drive from Woodbridge to Dulles Airport: about thirty miles up Virginia one twenty-three and the Fairfax County Parkway, around an hour.

holds.card: Dulles to Paris Charles de Gaulle, about 7½ hours
holds.text: Fly from Dulles across the Atlantic to Paris Charles de Gaulle: about three thousand eight hundred fifty miles, roughly seven and a half hours.

holds.card: Paris to Munich, through France and Germany
holds.text: In Paris, pick up a car for the longest drive of the trip: about seventeen hundred miles through eight countries. Head east past Metz and Strasbourg into Germany, then on through Stuttgart and Munich.

holds.card: Salzburg to Belgrade, through Austria, Slovenia and Croatia
holds.text: Cross into Austria at Salzburg, go under the Alps through the Karawanken Tunnel into Slovenia, then continue past Ljubljana and Zagreb to Belgrade, in Serbia.

holds.card: Belgrade to Istanbul, through Bulgaria and into Turkey
holds.text: From Belgrade, head southeast through Niš into Bulgaria, past Sofia and Plovdiv, then cross into Turkey at Edirne for the final run to Istanbul Airport.

holds.card: Istanbul to Osaka Kansai, about 11 hours
holds.text: From Istanbul, fly east across Asia to Osaka's Kansai Airport: about five thousand four hundred miles, roughly eleven hours.

holds.card: Osaka Kansai to Tokyo Haneda, past Nagoya and Shizuoka
holds.text: In Japan, drive from Kansai Airport to Tokyo's Haneda Airport: about three hundred forty miles of expressway past Nagoya, Shizuoka and Yokohama. Remember, Japan drives on the left.

holds.card: Tokyo Haneda to Los Angeles, about 10 hours
holds.text: From Haneda, fly across the Pacific to Los Angeles: about five thousand five hundred miles, roughly ten hours. You'll cross the International Date Line and gain back a day.

holds.card: Los Angeles to Albuquerque, on I-15 and I-40
holds.text: Finally, the drive home across America: about two thousand six hundred sixty miles. Leave Los Angeles on I fifteen and I forty, through Arizona past Flagstaff, and into New Mexico through Albuquerque.

holds.card: Amarillo to Memphis, across Texas, Oklahoma and Arkansas
holds.text: Stay on I forty across the Texas panhandle at Amarillo, through Oklahoma City, and across Arkansas to Memphis.

holds.card: Memphis to Woodbridge, via Nashville, Knoxville and I-81
holds.text: Then cross Tennessee past Nashville and Knoxville, take I eighty-one up the Shenandoah Valley into Virginia, and head home to Woodbridge.
